prerequisites.title: SurveyMonkey account
prerequisites.detail: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app. Competitors of SurveyMonkey may not open a Developer Account.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and terms
prerequisites.detail: Your app must include a privacy policy and terms of use. State whether users need an account with your service.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS and support
prerequisites.detail: All communication must use HTTPS with a valid certificate, and you must offer easily accessible support.

steps.title: Register a draft app
steps.detail: Log in to SurveyMonkey and register an app to get a client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Draft the minimal scope list and set each as required, optional or not required. Avoid the two approval-gated scopes if you can.
steps.done_when: Scopes are set in app settings.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret, then copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the SurveyMonkey app settings.

steps.title: Request approval for gated scopes
steps.detail: Contact the SurveyMonkey help center with details of your app and use case.

steps.title: Prepare the app listing
steps.detail: Draft an honest English listing with a non-generic name that omits 'SurveyMonkey' and versioning.

steps.title: Submit listing for approval
steps.detail: Use the listings tab in My Apps to submit.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey review
steps.done_when: App is approved and deployed as Public.

steps.title: Deploy and connect users
steps.detail: Deploy the app before the 90-day draft period ends. Each customer authorizes through OAuth and gets their own token.

traps.title: Public apps published in the App Directory can make
traps.detail: Public apps published in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

traps.title: Limits are enforced at 100% only after the app
traps.detail: Limits are enforced at 100% only after the app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days (up to 150% violations are permitted three times in a 30-day window).

traps.title: Draft app disabled after 90 days
traps.detail: A draft app must be deployed within 90 days or it is disabled. The help center can extend it.

traps.title: Private apps cannot serve other organizations
traps.detail: Private apps are limited to one account or Team. Outside customers need a Public app.

traps.title: No AI training on API data
traps.detail: You may not use API data to train or improve AI or machine learning systems. Check this against your agent design.

traps.title: Five sign-ins in three months
traps.detail: Public apps should have at least five OAuth sign-ins in the first three months.

traps.title: Approval can be refused
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey may reject an app on criteria not listed, and may remove it from the directory for any reason.

traps.title: Paid plans and tokens
traps.detail: Customers on Basic plans can read only 25 responses per survey. Some scopes ask them to upgrade, and tokens do not expire now but may later.

traps.title: Secret refresh revokes all access
traps.detail: Refreshing the app secret revokes all access to the app.

blockers.symptom: Customer is asked to upgrade during OAuth
blockers.what_it_means: Your app uses scopes tied to paid plans and the customer lacks that plan.
blockers.what_to_do: Mark those scopes optional, or tell customers a paid plan is needed.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review scopes and suggest which can be optional.

blockers.what_it_means: A Basic plan account asked for more than 25 responses.
blockers.what_to_do: Tell the customer to upgrade or limit requests to 25 responses.
blockers.agent_can_help: Handle the error in agent code.

blockers.what_it_means: The user revoked access, so you must repeat OAuth.

evidence.quote: You may not use SurveyMonkey’s Marks as part of the name of your company or of any App or other product or service created by you.
evidence.answer: The developer may not use SurveyMonkey's Marks as part of the name of the company or of any App or product.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your Apps must be clearly labeled as your own, and not SurveyMonkey’s.
evidence.answer: Apps must be clearly labeled as the developer's own and not SurveyMonkey's; the developer may not label its product as a SurveyMonkey product.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: you may not label your product as a SurveyMonkey product or use the Marks as part of your own logo
evidence.answer: The developer may not label its product as a SurveyMonkey product or use the Marks as part of its own logo.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your App must include a privacy policy and/or privacy notices which describe in reasonably adequate detail how you handle any User data and personally identifiable information that may be collected from Users via the API.
evidence.answer: Each App must include a privacy policy and/or privacy notices describing how it handles User data, and provide terms of use.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: To proxy the redirect, set the authorized redirect URI in your OAuth app's settings to your own endpoint, not Composio's.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The example redirect URI on your own domain is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio's callback URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio. The user's browser needs to be redirected so the OAuth flow completes correctly.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect; it must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: By default, the OAuth flow briefly redirects the browser through Composio's backend domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: Routing through your own domain is an option if you need to hide Composio's domain.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: Without your own OAuth app, the provider's consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' (example given for Google, GitHub, etc.); the page does not name SurveyMonkey.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Bringing your own OAuth app is recommended only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display Composio's callback URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: This is a general Composio page, not SurveyMonkey-specific. It says Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so the developer does not register one.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available. The page does not say whether SurveyMonkey has a managed app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config lets the developer supply their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You're building and iterating.** No OAuth app registration, no credentials to manage.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are a good fit while building and iterating, since no OAuth app registration or credential management is needed.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth. Fine for internal tools, prototypes, and development.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see 'Composio wants to access your account' on the OAuth consent screen. The page says this is fine for internal tools, prototypes, and development.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: Production apps that want users to see the developer's own app name on consent screens should use their own OAuth app instead of the managed app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes for managed apps may not include everything needed, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers. A developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You're connecting to a custom instance.** Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app rather than the managed one.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You don't have to pick one approach for all toolkits. Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: Developers can mix approaches: use their own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens, and managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: A managed app can still be white-labeled on the Connect Link page with the developer's logo and app title, without the developer's own OAuth app.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.
evidence.answer: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app (no separate developer program is mentioned).

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To use our API, you’ll need to register a draft app to your SurveyMonkey account.
evidence.answer: To use the API you register a draft app to your SurveyMonkey account.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.
evidence.answer: For Private apps, all users must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid plan that offers direct API access.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: No other SurveyMonkey accounts can authenticate a draft app.
evidence.answer: A draft app can only be authenticated by its owner; no other SurveyMonkey accounts can authenticate it.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Private apps don’t need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.
evidence.answer: Private apps (for use within one team) do not need any review by SurveyMonkey.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Every Public app must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey, and comply with terms of use, before it can be published in the App Directory (applies to Public apps; always triggered).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: For Public apps, two scopes (Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys) need SurveyMonkey's approval to use, which applies only when those scopes are used.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account and published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account once published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Before the 90-day draft period ends, you must deploy your app or it’ll be disabled.
evidence.answer: After the 90-day draft window, the app must be deployed as Public or Private, or it will be disabled.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.
evidence.answer: Private apps are restricted to users in one SurveyMonkey team, so they are not open to outside organizations.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: To get approval for the two approval-gated scopes on a Public app, the developer must contact SurveyMonkey's help center with details about the app and its use case.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Public apps use scopes to request permissions from app users during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Public apps request permissions through scopes during OAuth.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have SurveyMonkey paid plans.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys are the two scopes that require SurveyMonkey approval for Public apps.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote:
Create/Modify Responses |
Create or edit survey responses in your account |
responses_write |
Yes |
evidence.answer: The Create/Modify Responses scope is listed as requiring a paid plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: *Basic plan accounts can access response details for up to 25 responses per survey. Paid plans have unlimited access.
evidence.answer: The View Response Details scope is listed as requiring a paid plan for full access; Basic plan accounts get up to 25 responses per survey.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid SurveyMonkey plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, any accounts attempting to authenticate without the necessary plan will be asked to upgrade to proceed.
evidence.answer: If a Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, accounts without the plan are asked to upgrade before they can proceed.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Scopes can be set in the app settings as required, optional, or not required.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: All Draft and Private apps will initially be subject to request limits of 120 calls/minute and starting at 500 calls/day ( contact sales ).
evidence.answer: Draft and Private apps are subject to rate limits of 120 requests per minute and starting at 500 requests per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When a Public app is in draft (during development), it’s subject to draft request limits .
evidence.answer: A Public app in draft (during development) is subject to draft request limits.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Registering creates a draft app with an access token you can use to query against your account for 90 days.
evidence.answer: A draft app's access token can be used to query the account only for 90 days.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Public apps published in our App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day to our API.
evidence.answer: Public apps published in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We begin to enforce limits at 100% once your app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.
evidence.answer: Limits are enforced at 100% only after the app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days (up to 150% violations are permitted three times in a 30-day window).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Our access tokens don’t currently expire but may in the future.
evidence.answer: Access tokens do not currently expire, but may in the future; SurveyMonkey says it will warn developers before changes.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey will review all requests within 5 business days.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey says it will review requests for increased rate limits within 5 business days.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If your app is disabled, you must deploy it or contact us at our help center to request an extension.
evidence.answer: If a draft app is disabled for not being deployed in time, the developer can contact the help center to request an extension.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Private apps have API request limits and higher limits are available for purchase .
evidence.answer: Private apps have API request limits, and higher limits are available for purchase.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.
evidence.answer: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access .
evidence.answer: Private app users need a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Basic plans can retrieve up to 25 responses per survey
evidence.answer: Basic plans can retrieve up to 25 responses per survey; paid plans have unlimited response access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: If a Basic plan account requests more than 25 responses, the API returns error 1005 (402 Payment Required) with a message prompting to upgrade
evidence.answer: Accounts requesting more than 25 responses on a Basic plan receive error 1005 (402 Payment Required) prompting an upgrade.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The page presented to the user will identify your app, ask them to log into SurveyMonkey if they aren’t already, and ask them to authorize any required scopes .
evidence.answer: The customer is sent to an authorization page that asks them to log in and authorize the app's required scopes for their own account.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your app has required scopes , users will need to approve all of them and may need a paid SurveyMonkey plan to successfully OAuth into your app.
evidence.answer: Users must approve all required scopes, and may need a paid plan, for OAuth into the app to succeed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Your app will need to obtain additional access tokens for each SurveyMonkey account you wish to access.
evidence.answer: Each customer SurveyMonkey account needs its own access token obtained through OAuth.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Access tokens can be revoked by the user.
evidence.answer: The user can revoke an app's access token, after which the developer must complete OAuth again.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri URL encoded OAuth redirect URI you registered for your app (can be found and edited here )
evidence.answer: The redirect URI must be the OAuth redirect URI registered for the app, which can be found and edited in the app settings.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In that request, you’ll send us the code you received, along with your client secret, client ID, and redirect URI.
evidence.answer: During token exchange SurveyMonkey verifies the code, client secret, client ID and redirect URI.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Obtain this token in the Settings of your app in the MY APPS tab.
evidence.answer: For a Private app, the access token is obtained in the app's Settings in the MY APPS tab.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_id the unique SurveyMonkey client id you got when registering your app
evidence.answer: The client ID is the unique client id issued when the app is registered.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The client_secret can be found here .
evidence.answer: The client secret is found at a link on the authentication page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Scopes are configured in the app's settings as required, optional, or not required.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Private apps are subject to our terms of use .
evidence.answer: Private apps are subject to SurveyMonkey's terms of use; Public apps must also adhere to them.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: *Basic plan accounts can access response details for up to 25 responses per survey. Paid plans have unlimited access.
evidence.answer: Basic plan accounts are limited to 25 responses per survey for response-details access.
